links.reason: Padumai's 1405 verse has no marked speaker event and the marker calls its sense unsure; the 'deceiver' (வஞ்சனுக்கு) is not tied to Civakan's later leaving. In 1756 the word for Padumai (வாவிப்புண் அடையினாளை) is itself unclear, so the confirmation of her charge is a reconstruction.
links.text_issue: 1756 line 1 வாவிப்புண் அடையினாளை unclear; 1405 sense uncertain

links.reason: 49-50 say the soul is other than the body and that bound karma (வினை) is not its nature; they say nothing on how the stain is removed, so the 'epic leaves the end to the soul's own knowledge' is not in the Tamil. Tirumanthiram 117 (சூரியன் சந்நிதியிற் சுடுமாறு) is about the means of release, so the contrast is of different questions, not opposite answers.

1513 line 3 வண்டு கூறிய வண்ணம் அறிந்திலேன் does point back to the bee speech of 1502, so the link is real. But 1502 does not show it as 'his only farewell' and its sense is flagged uncertain, so 'proves to be' and 'part of her grief' are generous.

Both turn on vultures tearing the beautified body (பாறொடு நாய்கள் அசிப்ப ... / கோதையும் ... கழுகு குத்தும்), but Naladiyar 48 is not about a woman only; 'usually the woman's' is not in its Tamil, and the shared contemplation of carrion is an agreement, not a limit placed on it.

1097 (என் ... உணர்ந்த யானே ... இரங்கல் வேண்டா) and 269 (தம் வினைப் பயத்தின் ஆகும் ... இரங்கல்) give the same consolation, but 1097 does not answer or fulfil 269; the 'same usurper' and 'epic's own answer to tyranny' come from the plot, not from either verse.

1247 says the Jina ended karma (தீராவினை தீர்த்து) but nowhere says by his own effort alone, and it also says he led others (தீர்த்தந் தெரிந்துய்த்து); Tirumanthiram 1527 puts the end in grace once தன்செயல் அற்றால். The conflict rests on the marker's own reading, and the gains clause that the Saiva text 'agrees it cannot be ended by the soul alone' undercuts the claimed tension.

132 shows the king's wish (அரசினை விடுப்ப எண்ணி) and 150 the queen's feigned echo of it, a true contrast. But the verses do not use 'the same words', the pretence is known only from 152 outside the unit, and a feigned agreement is not an incompatible claim, so tension does not fit.

Both urge giving now because death can come (Nal 5 கூற்றம்; 139 சாதல் அஞ்சாய் ... அருஞ்சமம் வருகுவதாயின்), but 139 is a bard's plea for his own troupe and the Tamil of 11-12 is flagged unsure. 'Already a working plea' reverses the order of the two works, so teaches overstates it.

137 shows the kid-sacrifice for Chandikai being urged, and 259 ranks not killing above a thousand offerings, so the topic is shared. But the refusal that answers it is in 138-139, outside the unit, so the other-side gains clause is untrue of this pair, and 'qualifies' does not fit; it is the Kural's target illustrated.

Both give a daughter to the man who has done a deed; 440 is a public prize (தருதும் என்று கடிமுரசு இயம்ப) and 1339 a considered gift awaiting consent (நேருமாயின்). The contrast is true but it is a comparison of two scenes in one epic, not one unit answering or reversing the other.

The Paripadal fragment's woman wearing a floating garland (நாடு அறியப் பூ மாலை அப்பி) and Akananuru 296's friend scolding a man who bathed with another in the Vaigai are two unrelated poems on the same river. Nothing joins this woman to the 'dark girl', so 'how the gossip was made' is invented; lines 51-56 are also knotted.

317 says even able men (ஆற்றுவாரேனும்) who strike without a match (நிகரின்றி) are hurt, like a hand on stone; 473 blames those who rise on zeal not knowing their own strength (வலியறியார்). The proverb adds that the measure is against the foe, which the couplet only implies, so the pair teaches something and the note is accurate.

Kural 1137 praises not riding the palmyra horse (மடலேறா); 1028 is a parrot's claim that maidens hide their ailment from their nearest out of shame (நாணினாதலான்). Hiding an illness is not refusing the madal, and 'the silence the couplet praises' is not in the couplet; the pairing rests on a stretched shared theme of modesty.

The cited echo (நிலத்தோர் and gods wondering) is in 729, not in 731, which has only her garland, earrings and the line ending பாடத் தொடங்கினாள். The ending formula is shared, but whose songs came before, the hidden intent and the outcome of the garland are not in the Cintamani unit.

325 shows two gods-bound ascetics giving up the body (கழிந்தன உடலங்கள்) and 49 the proposal to do so (விடுதும் நம் உடலம்), a real fulfilment. But 325 is flagged unsure and whether this is the same pair is unsettled, and 'plan made under threat of the sword' is not in either verse.

2781 asks whose eyes would look on the wailing creature (தழுகின்றது ஆர் கண்ணே நோக்குமே) and 257 asks for flesh to be seen as another's wound (புண்); they meet on abstaining from flesh through pity, but the epic names no wound, so 'a name for what is being asked' is not true of it. The pair is thematic agreement.

1904 line 4 is hard (பிணங்குவார் ... வினைப் பிணக்கு) and 182 only says the Lord is hard to know (அறிவாரோ அரியரே); it does not say why. 'The earlier says why, the later says what follows' is an order the verses do not state, and the two are different kings addressing different hymns.

The only shared word is தொழுது, but in the Kural the others bow to eat (தொழுதுண்டு), a dependent's bow, while in 45 the sower folds his hands and speaks a wish to the seed (வீறொடு விளைக எனத் தொழுது). That a self-supporting farmer 'still bows' so his independence is dependence is built on one word.

Both show the stripping of ornaments in mourning (களைந்திடுவார் / நீக்கி), a repeated image. It is not a tension; and whose women these are in 2349 is not in the verse, so 'the usurper's own women' and 'price of the usurper's deed' rest on plot, while 295's வேந்தன் செய்த கொடுமை may blame either king.
links.text_issue: 295 sense uncertain; whose women in 2349 not stated

links.reason: 2910 says wise kings put anger aside and hide their wishes (வெளிப்படார் மறைத்தல்); Kural 590 forbids honouring a spy in public (சிறப்பறிய ஒற்றின்கண் செய்யற்க). Neither mentions the other's subject, and the gains clause of a 'working case' of showing favour betraying a secret is not in 2910. Shared theme of concealment only.

The epic gives the hedged valuation (மூன்றும் உறுவிலைத் தென்பவே, hearsay) and Naladiyar 46 dissects the body into parts, so the clash of valuations is real. But the narrator is not asserting it, the note does not say which reading the conflict depends on, and the arc to renunciation is brought from outside the verse.

1561 has the queen resolve to see the wedding (காண லுற்றாள்) and 1628 has her queens perform it, a plain fulfilment of an intent. But the king is not in either verse, so 'only attends' is invented, and the two units are consecutive in story order.

Both set pleasure beside doom (இன்பக் கடலிடை மூழ்கினான் / மறி குளகுண்டன்ன மகிழ்ச்சி). In 92 the only warning is இடங்கழிந்து; the shadow of slaughter comes from the plot, not the Tamil, so 'foreboding' is the reader's addition. The image of the lamb does fit a pleased king.

Both are herd-chief daughters given as prizes of a feat (440 ff. and Kalittokai's நல் ஏறு கொள்பவர்), a genuine custom link. But 102 never says the girl cannot be passed to another, so 'which the bull-catch does not allow' is invented, and an old-custom explanation of 440 is not shown by 489, whose ஏறங்கோள் is unclear.

63 (முன்னுயிர் உருவிற் கேதம்) and 321 (செய்த ... கொலை ... பவந்தோறும்) state the same doctrine, so 321 is a case of it. But the effigy and flour cock are not in the Tamil of 321, whose first line the marker calls provisional.

Both speak of pleasure that blinds, but 619 states only that the king knows neither sun nor moon (அறியான் களித்து); it does not say pleasure holds its own pain, nor a realm lost. Naladiyar 60 (இன்பம் ... இன்னாமை நோக்கி) is not developed by it, and the gains clause that 619 'only implies' the quatrain's judgment is not in the verse.

2557 does say tapas turns poison and the tusker aside and that spent tapas leaves no hiding (தவம் உலந்தால் ஆணில்லை), a real addition to 269's leaping past death. But the note misplaces hiding among the harms the strong escape, and the verse illustrates the claim rather than develops it; its sense is flagged unsure.

1155 is the courtiers' flattery that none can anger the discus-lord (யார் பிறர் உரைமின்), not a puzzle, so 1158 does not 'answer' it. 1158 gives a cause for the king's wrath, but the pair is consecutive story order and the rumour as fact (போலும் என்ற உரை) is read by the marker.

Both give the fruit of past deeds as a reason not to fret (670 வினைகள் ... இன்று நாம் அவலித்து என்ன; Nal 33 தொல்லைய தென்றுணர்வாரே). 670 then turns it into a reason to pay the overlord, a use the quatrain does not foresee, so the pair does show a limit to the maxim.

232 shows Fortune leaving Saccandan secretly (திருமகள் ஒளித்து நீங்க) but he is sunk in pleasure, not 'clinging' or 'grasping'; 2983 says Fortune stays with the one who lets go. The reversal is a real echo of Fortune's leaving, but the 'grasping king' is not in 232, and the logic of 2983 is flagged unsure.

Both use iron turned to gold (கறுத்த இரும்பே கனகமது / செம்பொனாகி), a real image link; 960 shows a rise in birth with no word of return, and 2051 adds மறித்து இரும்பாகா. 'Qualifies' does not fit, and the epic side's gain from 951 sits outside the unit.

Both name the one who subdued the five senses (ஐம்பொறியும் அட்டு / ஐந்தவித்தான்), but the Cintamani hymn is not a development of Kural 6, and 'evidence the couplet's sense-quencher was read as the Jina' is not shown by this verse. The other side gains nothing it did not have; this is a shared epithet.

1451 says the girl's sudden shame (கதுமென நாணப் பட்டான்) will mark the husband, and 1475 shows her gazing and turning her eyes away (வாட்கண் அகன்றாள்), so the later verse fulfils the earlier. The turning away is not said to be shame, but the reading is a fair one, and a prophecy and its event is the case the brief names.

497 ends பொய்யில் பொருளே பொருள் and 514 puts the words back in the same speaker's mouth as a reproach (பொருளைப் பொருள் என்று கொண்டாய்) after the wreck, so the creed is answered by its own speaker. The sense of both is flagged unsure, but the pun on பொருள் is in the Tamil and the opposition is real.

Both are about those at the Lord's feet (அடி தொழுதார் / அடிசேர்ந்தார்) and the end of birth, but 3091 does not use 'cross the sea' and the Kural's இறைவன் is not shown to be one who destroyed Desire and Death. The other-side gains clause imposes the Jain identification on the couplet, so the pair is an illustration.

Both give eight qualities (இருநான்கு குணமுடைய / எண்குணத்தான்), a number shared, not a distinctive image, and neither lists them. That 'a Jain poet can read the couplet as meaning his own lord' is not shown by the verse; the gains clause about the poet's reading is a guess.

118 (rule of heaven then earth) and 120 (gods then release) are in one hymn, and the ladder is the marker's reading across a verse outside the packet. The sequence is not an answering or fulfilling, and the prince's own kingship is not in either verse.

1922 names wealth as what makes the diminished into mountains (குன்றினார்களைக் குன்றென ஆக்கலும்), which Kural 751 gives as what makes persons of no account count; the epic's 'diminished' are fallen, not low, so wealth restores. Who they are is read from 1924, but the contrast with the couplet is in the Tamil.

119 has the low man beat the queen and 124 the king's reasons for sparing her (வதையினுக் குரிய ரல்லர்), but his reasons are rank and sex contempt, not restraint of mercy, as the marker says. Opposing acts are not incompatible claims, 'whose hand safer' is not a point of the poem, and the man's being her lover is from later verses.

1552 (ஊன் ... கழுகுண்ண ... உடல் சுமந்து) and 251 (தன்னூன் பெருக்கற்குத் தான் பிறிது ஊனுண்பான்) both turn on flesh fattened by flesh; the epic ends the fattened body as food for vultures, which the couplet leaves unsaid, and both attach it to the lack of அறம்/அருள். Both gains clauses hold.

2727 is Civakan's solitary reflection on strife and penance and 2988 his invitation to the wives to cross old deeds (தொல்வினை நீத்த நீந்தி); 2988 does not repeat the reflection. The pair is a resolve and its sequel in the same chapter, and 'thought then shared' is the story order, not a teaching.

78 praises the city for men not caught in the women's net (பெண் வலைப் படாதவர்), and 98 turns the moat into a courtesan that destroys whoever falls in (பட்டவர்த் தப்பலின் ... கணிகை), so the vice shunned becomes the defence. The sense of 98's syntax is flagged unsure, but the shared figure and its reversal are in the Tamil.

Kural 698 warns subjects not to belittle a king as young; in 703 the king belittles a prince's challenge (பிள்ளை ... அளியின் பிள்ளைதான் உரைத்த). The roles are reversed, the shared word is இளையை, and the verse has a misprint (விளையை), so the couplet is not what the verse shows.

999 puts the sea of longing and the madal in one verse (வேலை மாக்கடல் வேட்கை ... மடல் ஊர்தலை கருதினாள்) as Kural 1137 says a woman does not ride it though plunged in a sea of desire. Thinking of it shows the pressure the couplet names, so the pair tests the couplet.
